subject: QBR: launch readiness — scenario planning & risk heatmap
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: launch readiness — scenario planning & risk heatmap

Team —

As we prep for the QBR next week I want a concise, slide-ready view of launch readiness across product + eng for the next two customer launches (Orchard Health and the EU marketplace pilot). Please convert the current workstream status into three traffic scenarios we can walk the execs through:

- Scenario A — nominal load, SLA targets met;
- Scenario B — +2x peak traffic to reflect marketing burst (cost/latency trade-offs);
- Scenario C — degraded hw / fallback (what degrades and how we degrade gracefully).

Deliverables (due COB Fri, 19 Mar):
- Updated launch matrix (sheet: milestones, owner, gating flag) — attach as XLSX;
- Risk heatmap per scenario (one slide per scenario) — use attached template;
- Short mitigation plan with owners for top 5 delivery risks.

Key asks: call out any blocker that prevents an on-time 2027-04-05 go-live for Orchard Health and highlight where we need an SLA exception or business decision.

I attached a draft "launch-matrix-v2.xlsx" and the "risk-heatmap-template.pptx" to save time.

I’ll consolidate and produce a one-page exec view after your updates. If we need a quick 30-min sync before Friday, say when.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: launch readiness — scenario planning & risk heatmap

Marcus —

Quick status from product/launch side:

Progress:
- Milestones: feature freeze in place (2027-03-14). Integration tests against dedicated env are 65% green; currently tracking remaining items in the launch matrix.
- Docs: Orchard acceptance criteria captured in orchard-prod-plan.docx (shared in Drive).

Open delivery risks (top items):
1) Dedicated capacity scheduling: cloud vendor pricing window pushed our reserved slot from 3/28 to 4/03. If not resolved, we only get full capacity after customer go-live. Impact: Scenario B/C high.
2) Model compilation regression: a quantization path introduced a small tokenization mismatch for the conversational model. Engineering has a patch but we need validation across long-tail prompts — ETA 48 hours.
3) KMS/key escrow approval: customer legal asks for HSM-backed keys; security needs ~5 business days to onboard the KMS vendor once procurement gives the green light.

Mitigations proposed:
- For capacity, request temporary burst on hosted tier for the first 72 hours post-launch and plan a ramp to dedicated once capacity is available.
- Hold on the quantization changes for the release branch until the validation completes; revert if validation fails.
- Engage Tessa to accelerate KMS vendor checklist and confirm required docs.

I’ll update the launch-matrix-v2.xlsx with gating flags and owners by EOD Thu (18 Mar).

Laura
Product Director
Redwood Inference

Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: launch readiness — scenario planning & risk heatmap

Thanks Laura — quick engineering view and asks for the decisions we need to call out in the QBR.

Engineering mitigations and asks:
- Temporary burst: we can enable a hosted-tier burst for first 72 hours as Laura suggested. We need explicit approval from finance for incremental spend estimate (~$18k/day under Scenario B).
- Traffic shaping: implement request-level throttles and retry budgets for background ingestion pipelines during peak windows. Impact to latency: +30–50ms on average for customer-facing calls.
- Compilation/regression: will freeze the release branch and ship the safe model variant if validation is not complete by 18:00 PT Thu. That variant adds ~6% cost but avoids regressions.
- KMS onboarding: engineering can integrate HSM once vendor is approved; without vendor approval we must redact certain logs and adjust retention for PHI workflows.

Please confirm: do we want to present Scenario B as "marketing burst — accept latency/cost trade-off" or present it as "defer heavy-adoption features until dedicated capacity is provisioned"? I think the exec ask should be a single decision so we can present a clean runbook.

Vivek
VP Engineering
Redwood Inference

Adding the sales/CS perspective for Orchard Health go-live: 

Customer constraints:
- Orchard expects production access 2027-04-05 and has internal payer audits scheduled in the following two weeks; they require evidence of key rotation policy and audit logs before ramp.
- Procurement has returned the PO but DocuSign is pending a final sign-off from their security lead (link attached).

Commercial asks and risks: 
- If dedicated capacity slips beyond 4/05 we will need a temporary credit and a clear runbook for expected performance degradation; customer is unlikely to accept visible latency regressions without financial concession.
- Ask: explicit fallback behavior for PHI requests (redaction + manual review) so we can commit to compliance controls.

I'll coordinate a run-through with Jamie Park (Orchard) on Fri morning to walk them through the scenarios and get alignment on SLAs. If you can share the scenario slides prior to that call (Thu evening), that'd help de-risk the conversation.

Marissa
Enterprise AE
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the fast turns — summary and owners (I'll pull these into the QBR slides):

1) Capacity scheduling (owner: Laura): keep pursuing the reserved slot; parallel plan: finance approval for hosted-tier burst. Deliverable: decision & cost estimate by 2027-03-18 18:00 PT.
2) Model compilation (owner: Vivek): freeze release branch if validation incomplete; deliverable: validation results or revert decision by 2027-03-18 18:00 PT.
3) KMS onboarding (owner: Tessa): accelerate vendor checklist; deliverable: vendor approval path + list of required docs by 2027-03-22.
4) Customer compliance runbook (owner: Marissa): produce PHI fallback runbook and talk track for Orchard by 2027-03-19 12:00 PT.

Immediate asks I will present at the QBR: approval for a 72-hour hosted-tier burst (estimated incremental spend under Scenario B ~ $18k/day) and permission to ship the safe model variant if validation misses the cutoff. If we get both approvals, we can keep the go-live date at 2027-04-05 with controlled risk.

Next steps: please upload updated launch-matrix-v2.xlsx and the three scenario slides to the Drive folder (link below) by EOD Fri. I’ll run a 30-min QBR prep huddle:

- Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 10:00 PT
